newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse eases on publishers, power firm.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse eases on publishers, power firm.

text.p: A sharp fall in the share prices of Nation Printers & Publishers and Kenya Power & Lighting forced down the Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index, bourse officials said on Wednesday.
The index was down 35.78 points to 3439.15. Turnover was posted at 115.7 million shillings from 975,300 shares compared to 26 million shillings at 680,636 shares on Tuesday.
Nation Printers shed 65 shillings to close at 100 while Kenya Power lost 13 shillings to close at 155.
Nation adjusted after it traded "ex-all" -- without bonus or dividend -- for the first time on Wednesday.
The market was in a lull and would remain stagnant at least until interim results start creeping in July, brokers said.
"Caution is slowly creeping in," one broker said.

There was a mixed attitude to general elections sometime this year. Some investors wanted to wait until after the elections while some others actually thought they should buy now because prices were low, another broker said.
Meantime foreign investors continued to boost prices on selected key shares.
They bought Kenya Power & Lighting at a reserve price of 174 on the three-day offer board and Kenya Commercial Bank at between 96 and 98.50 from 96.
Barclays Bank was unchanged at 113 while Standard Chartered Bank edged a shilling to close at 47.50.
Total Kenya eased to 71 from 71.50 while Brooke Bond gained 3.0 to 125. Rea Vipingo was unchanged at 8.80. Uchumi Supermarket shed 50 cents to 40.25 while Kenya Airways closed at 8.15 from 8.05.
